title: GTA 6 | DÍA 2 MODO HISTORIA | DjMaRiiO
script:
There’s a detail buried in the description of this video that tells you more about the state of Grand Theft Auto VI right now than any screenshot ever could. Three euros. That’s the suggested contribution attached to getting your voice onto the screen.

The video is titled “GTA 6, Day 2, Story Mode,” and it comes from DjMaRiiO, a Spanish-language creator whose channel is best known for sports games, particularly the FIFA and EA Sports FC franchise. Day two implies a day one, which implies a series, which implies an audience that showed up for the first installment and came back for more. That’s the part worth paying attention to.

Here’s what the description actually confirms. Viewers can send in audio clips through a Streamlabs page linked to the channel, and there’s a suggested three-euro contribution attached, with the creator explicitly framing it as a way to cut down on spam. The clips appear on screen during the stream. That’s it. That’s the confirmed information available from the source material. Everything else — what happens in the video, whether the footage comes from a retail copy, a preview build, or something else entirely — isn’t something I can verify from what’s publicly attached to it, and I’m not going to guess.

So let’s talk about what is verifiable about GTA 6 itself, because that’s the context that makes a video like this matter.

Rockstar Games confirmed Grand Theft Auto VI was in development back in February 2022, in a brief statement that also acknowledged the disappointing leak of early development footage circulating online. The first trailer arrived in December 2023 and gave the series its first real look at Leonida, the fictional state, and Vice City, a setting fans had been asking about since Grand Theft Auto: Vice City shipped in 2002. The second trailer followed in May 2025. Rockstar has shifted the release date more than once since then, and if you want the current status, the only reliable source is Rockstar’s own newswire — not a video title, not a thumbnail.

That’s the tension at the heart of this entire genre of content. Rockstar has been extraordinarily guarded. There has been no official announcement of a story mode walkthrough, no sanctioned early access program, no creator partnership that would hand a mid-sized channel day two of the campaign. So when a title like this appears, it raises a question the thumbnail will never answer: what exactly are we looking at?

There are a few possibilities, and they’re worth separating cleanly. It could be a creator working from a leaked or datamined build, which does happen, and which Rockstar has historically answered with takedowns. It could be something else entirely — a piece of content whose relationship to the actual game is not clear from the public description. The point is not to accuse this specific video of anything. The point is that the description gives us no way to settle the question, and the title alone is a claim, not evidence.

That’s why the three-euro detail matters. It is concrete. It shows a creator building an interactive format around GTA VI content: viewers send audio, the creator screens it, the clips appear on screen, and a suggested contribution is framed as spam control. That is a real, verifiable piece of the GTA VI content ecosystem. It suggests demand for anything GTA VI-related is strong enough that creators are building participation mechanics around it, even while official information remains tightly controlled by Rockstar.

And that’s the larger story. A screenshot can be cropped, a thumbnail can be staged, a title can promise anything. But a Streamlabs link, a suggested contribution, and a stated reason for it are small, mundane, and specific. They tell you how the content is being made and how the audience is being invited in. They don’t tell you whether the footage is real. They don’t tell you what Rockstar has authorized. They don’t tell you what the game’s current release status is. For that, you still have to go to Rockstar’s own newswire.

The video may be Day 2 of something. But the only confirmed story here is the one in the description: a creator, a Streamlabs page, a suggested three-euro contribution, and clips on screen. Everything beyond that is a question the public material doesn’t answer.
